subject: Hosted API performance: p95/p99 spike — batching churn suspected
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex@finsight.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 latency across our workload hitting Redwood's hosted API starting at ~08:45 PDT. Error rate is elevated (~3% 5xx) and some requests are timing out. This began right after our morning traffic ramp — total QPS increased by ~20%.

Attached is a quick screenshot of our timeseries and a short request dump. Can you confirm whether any config or rollout happened on your side? We have a lot of production traffic and this is impacting SLAs for a handful of customers.

Priority: Sev2 — looking for immediate triage and mitigation steps.

Thanks,
Jordan
Lead SRE, Finsight

Attachments: p95_timeseries.png (image/png), request_dump_20270425.log (text/plain)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

Jordan — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We're not showing any config rollouts on the Hosted control plane at that time. I'm triaging with infra now.

Immediate asks:
- Can you share sample request IDs from the log (X-Request-Id) so we can trace them through our routing?
- Are you pinned to a specific model version or using the "latest" tag?

Initial hypothesis from cursory checks: we've observed increased batching churn in one of the top-end GPU pools which can produce queue starvation and bursty p95 regressions when QPS patterns change quickly. I'm looping in Sean and Karthik to validate runtime metrics and potential mitigation (temporary route throttling or pinning to a stable variant).

I'll update in 20 minutes.

—Mina
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

Thanks Mina. Quick snapshot from the serving runtime shows one GPU pool (gpupool-7) with oscillating queue depth and repeated batch re-assembly events between 08:42-09:00. See attached batching_summary.csv for per-pool stats.

Observations:
- Average batch utilization dropped while per-request latency spiked — classic batching churn where workers spin up and flush partially filled batches.
- KV cache hit rates look stable; not a cache regression.
- We see several model-variant fallbacks in the logs around 08:47 which coincide with higher error rates.

Short mitigations we can do asap:
1) Temporarily route Finsight traffic to gpupool-3 (steady state) — requires a short TTL change (1 minute rollout window).
2) Increase min-batch timeout threshold for gpupool-7 to reduce churn (may increase median latency slightly but should recover p95).

Recommend (1) for fastest customer relief and then (2) to stabilize. Looping Marissa for executive visibility in case we need credits/contract exceptions.

—Sean
Core Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: batching_summary.csv (text/csv)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex@finsight.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

Thanks Sean — sending two example X-Request-Id values from our dump: req_23a9f, req_23b0c. We're currently on model tag "gpt-open-1.1.2" (not pinned to a digest).

We appreciate the quick plan. Please confirm when the route change is in effect; we'll monitor from our side and can throttle client-side if needed.

-Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

I rolled the route change at 10:00 PDT directing Finsight's routing policy to gpupool-3 (stable pool) with a 1 minute step. Verified via the control plane that the live routing weight shifted to gpupool-3.

Preliminary results: within 90s p95 dropped from ~1.8s to ~420ms for sampled requests and 5xx errors trended back down. Leaving an elevated monitor for 30 minutes.

Next: I'll keep min-batch timeout on gpupool-7 increased by 25ms for the rest of the hour to prevent immediate churn while we investigate allocation triggers.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fw: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

Marissa — looping you in for visibility. Summary: Finsight saw a p95/p99 spike during the morning ramp; we traced to batching churn in gpupool-7. Route shifted to gpupool-3 and short-term mitigations applied. Customer impact reduced; keeping monitors up.

If finance/credits or a small SLA goodwill gesture is needed, let me know and I'll prepare notes. Also suggests we ticket this for a post-mortem focused on pool allocation policy and autoscaler thresholds — it looks like short lived spin-ups of new workers caused underfilled batches.

Best,
Mina
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan@finsight.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Sudden regression in p95/p99 for hosted API — started ~08:45 PDT

Appreciate the quick containment and clear notes. Action items for follow-up:
- Post-mortem by EOD tomorrow with timeline + root cause (Karthik/Sean)
- Short-term config guard: add a temporary autoscaler cooldown in production to reduce churn (Sean)
- Customer follow-up: Mina to send status summary and planned mitigations; offer one week of fee credit if impact confirmed in last 2 hours of the incident (Mina)

Jordan — we're committed to preventing recurrences. Mina will send a summary and we'll loop legal/finance if we need to formalize any credit.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
